results.content: Investors were rattled this week as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield soared to its highest level since 2007, but sticky inflation is just one of the factors behind this latest surge. The key 10-year Treasury yield, which influences mortgages, leapt to 5.23% on Friday for its highest level since 2007. The 10-year yield's rapid climb above 5% shows how quickly investors' expectations have shifted toward additional tightening from the Federal Reserve in light of stubborn inflation. Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said one more interest-rate hike “late this year” may be appropriate to help contain inflation, prompting investors to dial back their expectations for an increase in October just before midterm elections. Williams underscored the point by saying there was no urgency to act following the central bank’s decision to lift rates earlier this month.

results.content: Bond traders priced in a later start to further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes on indications of weakness in the US labor market. September employment data showing the US added fewer jobs than economists estimated eroded expectations for a rate hike this month or in December. They rebounded, however, and were more than a basis point higher on the day near 4.81% by late morning in New York, as the outlook for three hikes by the end of next year to battle inflation remained intact. Interest-rate swaps showed traders priced in about a 20% chance that the Fed lifts benchmark borrowing costs at its October meeting, compared to nearly 30% prior to the data. results.title: US consumer sentiment deteriorates in September, inflation expectations rise By Reuters

results.content:
A local shopper searches for meat products Sept. 21, 2026, at the Market 32 supermarket in South Burlington. (Robert Nickelsberg/Getty Images) · Robert Nickelsberg via Getty Images

 

As inflation remained elevated in August and the war with Iran continues, Americans' outlook for inflation in the year ahead jumped to 4.6% in September from 4% in August, marking the highest reading since June.

It's also far higher than inflation expectations of 3.4% seen in February and all readings in 2024.

results.content:
The survey's measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the ​next year jumped ​to ⁠4.6% from 4.0% last month. Twelve-month inflation expectations were at 3.4% in ​February before the U.S.-led war ​with ⁠Iran started. Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years edged up 3.4% from ⁠3.3% ​in August. They are ​higher than their 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.

Reporting ​By Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama
